title: 25BT056: Basket Study of Viral Cytotoxic T Lymphocytes
off: 25BT056: Basket Study of Viral Cytotoxic T Lymphocytes in Children, Adolescents and Young Adults With Viral Infection Following Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant, Solid Organ Transplant or in Primary Immunodeficiencies
summary:
This study is evaluating the safety and effectiveness of virus-specific cytotoxic T lymphocytes (vCTLs) for treating difficult-to-control viral infections caused by cytomegalovirus (CMV), adenovirus (ADV), Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), or BK virus in children, adolescents, and young adults with weakened immune systems. Eligible participants include recipients of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, solid organ transplantation, and patients with primary immunodeficiency disorders.

vCTLs are immune cells collected from a related donor and selected to recognize and fight specific viruses. The cells are manufactured using the CliniMACS® Cytokine Capture System and administered by intravenous infusion. Additional infusions may be given if viral infection persists.

The study will assess the safety of vCTL therapy, including the risk of graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) and infusion-related reactions, as well as its ability to reduce viral infection, improve clinical outcomes, and support survival. Participants will be monitored for approximately 12 weeks after their final vCTL infusion. Participants will all receive vCTLs; there is no comparison group.

Participants will:

1. Have donor-derived vCTLs manufactured for infusion using the CliniMACS Cytokine Capture System
2. Receive the vCTLs through an intravenous infusion
3. Be monitored for side effects and infusion reactions, viral levels through blood testing, clinical outcomes, including response to treatment, survival, and time without detectable virus
desc:
Viral infection and reactivation are major causes of morbidity and mortality in individuals with inherited or acquired immunodeficiency, including recipients of allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant and solid organ transplant. Cytomegalovirus, adenovirus, Epstein-Barr virus, and BK virus may cause severe, persistent, or progressive disease. Standard antiviral therapies may be ineffective, poorly tolerated, contraindicated, or limited by viral resistance.

This is a single-institution, open-label, prospective pilot basket study of donor-derived virus-specific cytotoxic T lymphocytes for treatment of refractory CMV, adenovirus, EBV, and/or BK virus infection. The vCTL product is manufactured from an adult related donor with at least a 3/6 human leukocyte antigen (HLA) match to the recipient. Following leukapheresis, donor cells are stimulated with virus-specific peptide pools and enriched for interferon-gamma-secreting T cells using the CliniMACS Cytokine Capture System on the CliniMACS Prodigy platform.

Participants will receive vCTLs by slow intravenous push. Dose is based on donor-recipient HLA matching. Additional infusions of the same dose may be administered every 2 weeks for persistent detectable viral replication, up to a maximum of five infusions, provided safety and redosing criteria are met.

Safety will be evaluated in aggregate across all viral cohorts, with particular focus on Grade 3 or higher acute graft-versus-host disease and Grade 3 or higher infusion-related reactions considered at least possibly related to vCTL infusion. Antiviral efficacy will be evaluated separately by virus type using quantitative polymerase chain reaction and clinical response assessments. Participants will be followed through 12 weeks after their final vCTL infusion.
elig:
Recipient Inclusion Criteria

1. Subjects with inherited (e.g. SCID) or acquired immunodeficiency with evidence of refractory viral infection with one or more of CMV, adenovirus, EBV, or BK virus. Specifically:

   1. Increasing viremia by quantitative PCR with increase from baseline over 7 days, or persistent detection after 14 days despite appropriate standard of care therapy (e.g. anti-viral therapy, withdrawal of immunosuppression), AND/OR
   2. Progressive symptomatic viral infection evidenced by persistent clinical symptoms or end-organ disease attributable to the viral infection that has not improved after at least 7 days of appropriate standard-of-care therapy, or develops new clinical manifestations despite standard-of-care therapy, AND/OR
   3. Antiviral resistance, or inability to receive appropriate antiviral therapy due to intolerance, toxicity, contraindication, or lack of a feasible antiviral treatment option.
2. Age 0 - 29 years at time of consent
3. Female subjects of reproductive potential, defined per Oncology clinical guidelines as all females ≥ 12 years old, or \<12 years old who have reached menarche, must have a negative urine or serum pregnancy test. Testing may be performed using serum human chorionic gonadotropin (HCG) or urine
4. Subjects with reproductive potential must agree to use an effective method of birth control

Recipient Exclusion Criteria

1. Subjects with ≥ Grade 2 acute GVHD or moderate to severe chronic GVHD at the time of vCTL infusion
2. Subjects receiving systemic steroids (\> 0.5mg/kg/day prednisolone equivalent) at the time of vCTL infusion
3. Receipt of donor lymphocyte infusion within the 4 weeks preceding vCTL infusion
4. Receipt of thymoglobulin, alemtuzumab, or other T cell immunosuppressive monoclonal antibody within the 4 weeks preceding vCTL infusion
5. End-organ involvement of virus in sites that may, in the opinion of the investigator, put the subject at risk of unacceptable toxicity e.g. retinitis, cerebritis, encephalitis
6. Known HIV infection
7. Any medical condition which could compromise participation in the study, in the opinion of the investigator
8. Female subjects who are pregnant or breastfeeding

Donor Inclusion Criteria

1. Age ≥ 18 years old
2. HLA match with the recipient of at least 3/6. Donor may be the original transplant donor or a third party donor
3. Consent to pre screening with PepTivator testing of T cell response to the relevant virus(es)
4. Willing to undergo formal donor evaluation equivalent to that required for hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) donors
5. Willing to consent to T cell processing under CHOP protocol CHP784 (IRB 04 004078) using the CliniMACS device

Donor Exclusion Criteria

1. Donors younger than 18 years old
2. HLA match with the recipient less than 3/6
3. Refusal or inability to consent to PepTivator pre screening
4. Unwillingness or inability to undergo formal donor evaluation (as required for HSCT donors)
5. Refusal or inability to consent to T cell processing under The Children's Hospital of Philadelphia protocol (CHP784, IRB 04 004078) using the CliniMACS device
6. Any medical, infectious, or other condition identified during evaluation that contraindicates donation per standard HSCT donor eligibility guidelines (e.g., active uncontrolled infection, significant cardiopulmonary disease, pregnancy) or that would preclude safe apheresis/T cell collection as determined by the evaluating clinicians.

arms.d: Participants with refractory CMV, ADV, EBV, and/or BK virus will receive donor-derived virus-specific cytotoxic T lymphocytes. Participants may receive a multivirus-specific product when clinically indicated. The initial infusion is administered on Day 0. Repeat infusions may be administered every 2 weeks, up to five total infusions, for ongoing detectable viral replication if eligibility criteria are met.

primary.m: Occurrence of Grade 3 or higher acute graft-versus-host disease (GVHD)
primary.tf: From first vCTL infusion (Day 0) through 12 weeks after the final vCTL infusion

primary.m: Occurrence of Grade 3 or higher infusion-related reactions
